entries.title: Water-borne illness in the rains
entries.summary: Across India, May to August account for over half of reported diarrhoeal disease outbreaks, and cholera outbreaks rise sharply with the monsoon, June to September. Typhoid and gastroenteritis are common in the monsoon.

sources.name: Dandabathula et al., Impact assessment of Swachh Bharat Mission on acute diarrheal disease outbreaks (IDSP data 2010-2018), J Family Med Prim Care 2019
Muzembo et al., Cholera outbreaks in India, 2011-2020: a systematic review, Int J Environ Res Public Health 2022
NCVBDC (MoHFW), National Guidelines for Clinical Management of Dengue Fever 2023

entries.title: Influenza, monsoon peak
entries.summary: Influenza circulates all year. Surveillance in Delhi, Lucknow, Nagpur, Pune, Kolkata, Dibrugarh and Alappuzha found the main peak in July to September, during the monsoon.

sources.name: Chadha et al. (ICMR-NIV), Dynamics of influenza seasonality at sub-regional levels in India and implications for vaccination timing, PLoS One 2015
Koul et al., Differences in influenza seasonality by latitude, northern India, Emerg Infect Dis 2014

entries.title: Japanese encephalitis season
entries.summary: In districts where Japanese encephalitis is endemic (outside Assam), cases usually start in July and peak in September and October, with transmission continuing into the post-monsoon months.

sources.name: NCVBDC (MoHFW), Operational Guidelines, National Programme for Prevention and Control of JE/AES
NCVBDC, What is the extent of problem of Japanese Encephalitis in India and control activities of JE

entries.title: Dengue and chikungunya
entries.summary: Dengue cases rise every year from July to November and peak after the monsoon; laboratory positivity is highest in September and October. Western and southern states also see cases all year. Chikungunya occurs mainly in the rainy season.

sources.name: NCVBDC (MoHFW), National Guidelines for Clinical Management of Dengue Fever 2023
Murhekar et al. (ICMR VRDL network), Epidemiology of dengue fever in India based on laboratory surveillance data 2014-2017, Int J Infect Dis 2019
NCVBDC (MoHFW), Guidelines for containment of chikungunya and dengue epidemic outbreaks

entries.title: Malaria, rainy season
entries.summary: In most parts of India malaria cases are highest in the rainy season, from July to November.

sources.name: NCVBDC (MoHFW), National Strategic Plan: Malaria Elimination 2023-27
Data For India, Malaria in India (quotes the NCVBDC National Strategic Plan 2023-27 on seasonality), 17 December 2024

entries.title: Nor'wester thunderstorms
entries.summary: Severe pre-monsoon thunderstorms, known locally as Kalbaisakhi, form over eastern and north-eastern India from March to May, bringing heavy showers, lightning, hail, squalls and dust storms.

sources.name: Tyagi, Sikka, Goyal and Bhowmick, A satellite based study of pre-monsoon thunderstorms (Nor'westers) over eastern India, MAUSAM 63(1), 2012 (IMD)

entries.title: Kyasanur Forest Disease season
entries.summary: In forest areas of the Western Ghats in Karnataka, Kerala, Goa and Maharashtra, Kyasanur Forest Disease occurs mainly in the dry months, December to June, with cases peaking from January to April.

sources.name: Bohra et al., Kyasanur Forest Disease virus: epidemiological insights, Viruses 2025
Oliveira et al., Geospatial clustering, seasonal trend and forecasting of Kyasanur Forest Disease in Goa, 2015-2018, Trop Med Health 2020
Kiran et al., Kyasanur Forest Disease outbreak and vaccination strategy, Shimoga District, 2013-2014, Emerg Infect Dis 2015
Murhekar et al. (ICMR), On the transmission pattern of Kyasanur Forest disease in India, Infect Dis Poverty 2015

entries.title: Cyclone season, post-monsoon
entries.summary: October to December is the main cyclone season, peaking in November. Bay of Bengal storms outnumber Arabian Sea ones about 4 to 1. In this season most landfalls from 1971 to 2020 were on the Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu coasts; on the west coast, Gujarat is most exposed.

sources.name: IMD RSMC New Delhi, Frequently Asked Questions on Tropical Cyclones and Marine Weather Services
Raj, Balachandran, Amudha and Geetha, Understanding and prediction of Indian northeast monsoon over the years, MAUSAM 76(1), 2025 (IMD)

entries.title: Cyclone season, pre-monsoon
entries.summary: A second cyclone season comes before the monsoon, from late April to early June, with a secondary peak in May. Cyclones in May and June can be of severe intensity.

sources.name: IMD RSMC New Delhi, Frequently Asked Questions on Tropical Cyclones and Marine Weather Services

entries.title: Pre-monsoon heat
entries.summary: Heat waves are most likely from March to June, with May the peak month. Hot weather lasts until the monsoon arrives: mid June in Bihar, about 30 June in Delhi and Punjab, and about 8 July in west Rajasthan.

sources.name: IMD, FAQ on Heat Wave
NCDC (MoHFW), Advisory for State Health Departments for Summer 2026, NPCCHH
IMD, Normal dates of onset/progress and withdrawal of the southwest monsoon over India (Pai et al., CRS Research Report 3/2020)

entries.title: South-west monsoon
entries.summary: The monsoon reaches east Bihar around 15 June and Delhi, Punjab, Haryana and east Rajasthan by about 30 June. It starts withdrawing from west Rajasthan around 17 September and leaves most of the region by 1 to 10 October.

sources.name: IMD, Normal dates of onset/progress and withdrawal of the southwest monsoon over India (Pai et al., CRS Research Report 3/2020)
NCVBDC (MoHFW), National Guidelines for Clinical Management of Dengue Fever 2023

entries.title: Dengue and chikungunya
entries.summary: Dengue cases usually start rising in July, peak in September and October and fall away by December. Chikungunya also occurs mainly in the rainy season.

sources.name: Singh and Chaturvedi, Temporal variation and geospatial clustering of dengue in Delhi, India 2015-2018, BMJ Open 2021
NCVBDC (MoHFW), National Guidelines for Clinical Management of Dengue Fever 2023
NCVBDC (MoHFW), Guidelines for containment of chikungunya and dengue epidemic outbreaks

entries.title: Hepatitis A and E
entries.summary: In Uttar Pradesh hospital studies, hepatitis A peaked before the monsoon, in May and June, while hepatitis E occurred all year with outbreaks peaking in the monsoon and post-monsoon months.

sources.name: Gupta et al., Hepatitis A and E in rural northern India (AIIMS Raebareli), Front Public Health 2026
Hassaan et al., HEV prevalence, risk factors and outcomes in a tertiary care hospital of Uttar Pradesh (Aligarh), Iran J Microbiol 2026

entries.title: Litchi-season AES, north Bihar
entries.summary: In Muzaffarpur, India's largest litchi-growing area in north Bihar, outbreaks of acute encephalopathy in children have been reported in many years. In 2014, cases linked to litchi toxins and low blood sugar were admitted from late May to mid July.

sources.name: Shrivastava et al. (NCDC and US CDC), Acute toxic encephalopathy and litchi consumption in an outbreak in Muzaffarpur, 2014, Lancet Glob Health 2017

entries.title: Influenza, winter rise
entries.summary: Besides the monsoon peak, India often sees a second influenza rise from January to March. Rajasthan had a large influenza A(H1N1) surge in January and February 2015.

sources.name: Vashishtha and Kumar, Optimizing influenza vaccine protection in India, Indian Pediatrics 2025
Sharma et al., Mortality due to influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 at a tertiary care hospital in Jaipur, January and February 2015, J Assoc Physicians India 2015

entries.title: Smog and poor air season
entries.summary: Air quality across the Indo-Gangetic plain usually worsens from October. Paddy stubble burning in Punjab, Haryana and the NCR districts of Uttar Pradesh adds smoke in October and November, and cold, still air traps pollution through December and January.

sources.name: PIB (MoEFCC), Parliament question: Air pollution caused by stubble burning
Shankar and Gadi, Variation in air quality over Delhi region: a comparative study for 2019 and 2020, Aerosol Sci Eng 2022
Centre for Science and Environment, Decoding winter air pollution in Indo-Gangetic Plain (analysis of CPCB monitoring data), January 2021
IMD, Press release: Seasonal outlook for the cold weather season, December 2025 to February 2026 (1 December 2025)
NCDC (MoHFW), Handbook for ASHA: Air pollution and its impact on health, 2024

entries.title: Winter and cold waves
entries.summary: December and January are the coldest months in north India, and cold waves are most frequent over the north-west plains. Cold spells raise health risks for older people, children and people with chronic illness. Early-morning fog can disrupt travel.

sources.name: IMD, FAQ on Cold Wave
IMD, Press release: Seasonal outlook for the cold weather season, December 2025 to February 2026 (1 December 2025)

entries.title: Winter cold
entries.summary: December and January are the coldest months across northern India. In hill areas IMD declares a cold wave when the minimum temperature falls to 0°C or below. Wind chill adds to the risk.

sources.name: IMD, FAQ on Cold Wave
IMD, Press release: Seasonal outlook for the cold weather season, December 2025 to February 2026 (1 December 2025)

entries.title: Influenza, winter peak
entries.summary: In Kashmir influenza follows a temperate pattern and peaks from January to March, unlike the plains, where the main peak comes with the monsoon.

sources.name: Koul et al., Differences in influenza seasonality by latitude, northern India, Emerg Infect Dis 2014

entries.title: South-west monsoon
entries.summary: The monsoon usually reaches Uttarakhand, Ladakh and most of Jammu and Kashmir by about 30 June and covers all of north-west India by about 8 July. It withdraws from the hill states by about 1 October.

sources.name: IMD, Normal dates of onset/progress and withdrawal of the southwest monsoon over India (Pai et al., CRS Research Report 3/2020)

entries.title: Scrub typhus and leptospirosis
entries.summary: In Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh, scrub typhus is seen mostly from July to November, with most cases in August to October. In the Kangra area, leptospirosis also peaks in September and October.

sources.name: Bhargava et al., Scrub typhus in Uttarakhand and adjoining Uttar Pradesh: seasonality, clinical presentations and predictors of mortality, Indian J Med Res 2016

entries.title: Pre-monsoon heat
entries.summary: Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Telangana are among the heat wave prone states. Heat waves are most likely from March to June, peaking in May, until the monsoon arrives in mid to late June.

sources.name: IMD, FAQ on Heat Wave
NCDC (MoHFW), Advisory for State Health Departments for Summer 2026, NPCCHH
IMD, Normal dates of onset/progress and withdrawal of the southwest monsoon over India (Pai et al., CRS Research Report 3/2020)

entries.title: South-west monsoon
entries.summary: The monsoon reaches Telangana and south Chhattisgarh by about 15 June and most of Madhya Pradesh by about 30 June. It withdraws from west Madhya Pradesh around 1 October and from Telangana and Chhattisgarh by about 15 October.

sources.name: IMD, Normal dates of onset/progress and withdrawal of the southwest monsoon over India (Pai et al., CRS Research Report 3/2020)
NCVBDC (MoHFW), National Guidelines for Clinical Management of Dengue Fever 2023

entries.title: Malaria
entries.summary: Malaria cases rise with the rains. Chhattisgarh's surveillance data for 2015 to 2023 show peaks in July and again in November, with the highest incidence in the Bastar and Surguja regions.

sources.name: Gahwai et al., Epidemiology of malaria in Chhattisgarh: IDSP surveillance data analysis 2015-2023, Trans R Soc Trop Med Hyg 2025
NCVBDC (MoHFW), National Strategic Plan: Malaria Elimination 2023-27
Data For India, Malaria in India (quotes the NCVBDC National Strategic Plan 2023-27 on seasonality), 17 December 2024

entries.title: Winter and cold waves
entries.summary: Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Telangana are among the cold wave prone states. The most cold wave days are seen over the plains of north-west and adjoining central India, in the December to February winter.

sources.name: IMD, FAQ on Cold Wave
IMD, Press release: Seasonal outlook for the cold weather season, December 2025 to February 2026 (1 December 2025)

entries.title: Pre-monsoon heat
entries.summary: Jharkhand, Odisha and West Bengal are among the heat wave prone states. Heat waves are most likely from March to mid June, peaking in May, until the monsoon arrives around mid June.

sources.name: IMD, FAQ on Heat Wave
NCDC (MoHFW), Advisory for State Health Departments for Summer 2026, NPCCHH
IMD, Normal dates of onset/progress and withdrawal of the southwest monsoon over India (Pai et al., CRS Research Report 3/2020)

entries.title: South-west monsoon
entries.summary: The monsoon covers most of West Bengal and Odisha by about 15 June and Jharkhand by about 20 June. It withdraws from Jharkhand around 10 October and from Odisha and the rest of the region by about 15 October.

sources.name: IMD, Normal dates of onset/progress and withdrawal of the southwest monsoon over India (Pai et al., CRS Research Report 3/2020)
NCVBDC (MoHFW), National Guidelines for Clinical Management of Dengue Fever 2023

entries.title: Malaria
entries.summary: In Kalahandi district of Odisha malaria occurs all year, but cases track rainfall and are highest in the peak rainy months, July to September. Nationally, malaria is highest from July to November.

sources.name: Panigrahi et al., Role of climatic factors on the perennial malaria cases in Kalahandi district of Odisha, J Vector Borne Dis 2025
NCVBDC (MoHFW), National Strategic Plan: Malaria Elimination 2023-27

entries.title: Dengue
entries.summary: In Kolkata about 90% of dengue cases fall in a yearly post-monsoon peak from August to November, two to three months after the heaviest rain. National data show the same post-monsoon rise.

sources.name: Rani Jena et al., Spatio-temporal distribution of dengue cases and vectors in Kolkata, 2017-2022, Emerging Microbes and Infections 2025
NCVBDC (MoHFW), National Guidelines for Clinical Management of Dengue Fever 2023

entries.title: Winter and cold waves
entries.summary: West Bengal, Jharkhand and Odisha are among the cold wave prone states. Cold waves fall in the December to February winter.

sources.name: IMD, FAQ on Cold Wave
IMD, Press release: Seasonal outlook for the cold weather season, December 2025 to February 2026 (1 December 2025)

entries.title: South-west monsoon
entries.summary: The monsoon reaches most of the north-east by about 5 June, among the earliest in India, and withdraws from the whole region by about 15 October.

sources.name: IMD, Normal dates of onset/progress and withdrawal of the southwest monsoon over India (Pai et al., CRS Research Report 3/2020)

entries.title: Malaria
entries.summary: In the north-eastern states the malaria transmission season starts early, around March. In Assam and Arunachal Pradesh just over half of all cases are reported in the monsoon months.

entries.title: Japanese encephalitis, Assam pattern
entries.summary: Assam reports 30 to 50% of India's JE cases. Unlike other endemic states, cases start appearing from February and peak in July; in upper Assam cases cluster in the rainy months, June to August.

entries.summary: Mizoram and Meghalaya report the most scrub typhus in national surveillance data. In Mizoram cases peak from August to October.

entries.title: Winter and cold waves
entries.summary: Sikkim, Assam and Tripura are among the cold wave prone states. Gangtok holds India's longest recorded cold wave spell, 17 days in December 1986.

sources.name: IMD, FAQ on Cold Wave

sources.name: IMD, FAQ on Heat Wave

entries.title: South-west monsoon
entries.summary: The monsoon reaches Goa by about 10 June, Mumbai by about 15 June, south Gujarat by about 20 June and most of Gujarat by about 30 June. It withdraws from Gujarat around 1 October and from Maharashtra and Goa by about 15 October.

entries.title: Leptospirosis
entries.summary: Leptospirosis outbreaks are reported from coastal Gujarat and Maharashtra and from Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, with cases in Goa. Cases start with the rains, decline as they recede, are more common post-monsoon, and floods can set off outbreaks.

entries.title: Winter and cold waves
entries.summary: Gujarat and Maharashtra are among the cold wave prone states. Cold waves fall in the December to February winter, and older people, children and people with chronic illness are most at risk.

sources.name: IMD, FAQ on Cold Wave
IMD, Press release: Seasonal outlook for the cold weather season, December 2025 to February 2026 (1 December 2025)

entries.title: Pre-monsoon heat
entries.summary: Heat waves can occur from March until the monsoon arrives in early June. Parts of Karnataka are heat wave prone, and heat waves occasionally reach Kerala.

sources.name: IMD, FAQ on Heat Wave
NCDC (MoHFW), Advisory for State Health Departments for Summer 2026, NPCCHH

entries.title: South-west monsoon
entries.summary: The monsoon sets in over Kerala around 1 June, covers coastal and south interior Karnataka by about 5 June and most of Karnataka by about 10 June. It withdraws from north Karnataka by mid October.

sources.name: IMD, Normal dates of onset/progress and withdrawal of the southwest monsoon over India (Pai et al., CRS Research Report 3/2020)

entries.title: North-east monsoon
entries.summary: From mid October the north-east monsoon brings further rain to Kerala and south interior Karnataka, more than half of it in October. October to December gives Kerala about 17% of its yearly rain.

sources.name: Raj, Balachandran, Amudha and Geetha, Understanding and prediction of Indian northeast monsoon over the years, MAUSAM 76(1), 2025 (IMD)
